notes.text: Admin: the problem set due Friday now runs to Monday, there is no class a week from Thursday because he is at a workshop, and office hours move to Wednesday two to four.
notes.quote: the problem set that was due Friday is now due Monday

notes.text: Almost all of today comes from the Cohen, Rosenfeld and Kolter paper, which is on the reading list.
notes.quote: Almost everything today is from the Cohen, Rosenfeld and Kolter paper. It's on the reading list.

notes.text: He placed this lecture as the point where the course stops playing whack-a-mole with empirical attacks and starts proving things instead.
notes.quote: this is the lecture where we stop playing whack a mole

notes.text: You are not defending the classifier you trained but a blurred copy of it, and the blurring is what buys the guarantee: a tiny push cannot cross a smeared decision boundary.
notes.quote: You are defending a blurred version of it, and the blurring is what buys you the guarantee

notes.text: He called randomized smoothing the same trick as label smoothing in a different costume: different literature, same instinct not to trust the sharp thing.
notes.quote: the same trick as label smoothing wearing a completely different costume

notes.text: The noisy copies are a batch of about a hundred thousand per input, so prediction runs four orders of magnitude slower than a forward pass, which is why certified numbers are rare in papers.
notes.quote: prediction is about four orders of magnitude slower than a forward pass

notes.text: The slide only fixes when the noise level is chosen; he added that the base classifier must itself be trained on noisy inputs at that same sigma, or smoothing a clean-trained model gives garbage.
notes.quote: you train with Gaussian augmentation at the same sigma you are going to certify at

notes.text: The margin becomes a radius only because the vote is a probability and probabilities under a Gaussian carry a geometry; the next slide makes that exchange rate explicit.
notes.quote: the vote is a probability, and probabilities under a Gaussian have a geometry

notes.text: Drawing more noise samples tightens the estimate of the vote probability but does not change it, so more samples cannot buy a bigger radius.
notes.quote: More samples tighten your estimate of the probability, they don't change the probability

notes.text: slide says noise at prediction time but he keeps saying you also train with it - same sigma both places
The vote probability is the chance the base classifier returns the top class on one single noise draw, not the majority over many draws.
notes.quote: It is the probability that the base classifier returns the top class when you draw one single noise sample

notes.text: why Phi inverse and not a tail bound?
notes.answer: Neyman-Pearson makes the worst case a half space, and the distance from a Gaussian's centre to a half space of a given mass is exactly Phi inverse, so it is exact rather than a bound.

notes.text: Phi inverse rather than a Hoeffding tail bound because Neyman-Pearson makes the worst case a half space, and the distance from a Gaussian's centre to a half space of given mass is exactly Phi inverse.
notes.quote: the distance from the centre of a Gaussian to a half space of a given mass is exactly fee inverse of that mass

notes.text: A tail bound would be true but loose, and loose here means throwing away radius you had already earned.
notes.quote: It would just be loose, and loose here means you throw away radius that you actually earned

notes.text: Pushed far enough the trade-off ends in collapse: the base classifier can no longer see anything and the vote probability falls to chance.
notes.quote: at some point the base classifier can't see anything at all and the vote probability collapses to chance

notes.text: The paper sweeps sigma at 0.25, 0.5 and 1, and the 0.5 curve is the one everybody ends up plotting.
notes.quote: they sweep sigma at point two five, point five and one, and the point five curve is the one everybody ends up plotting

notes.text: The certificate is an ell two guarantee even though the slide states the threat model in the ell infinity norm, because Phi inverse of a Gaussian mass is a Euclidean distance.
notes.quote: the certificate we just derived is an ell two certificate. Fee inverse of a Gaussian mass is a Euclidean distance

notes.text: You can convert, since an ell two ball of radius r contains an ell infinity ball of radius r over root d, but that root d is brutal once d is a real image.
notes.quote: An ell two ball of radius r contains an ell infinity ball of radius r over root d

notes.text: When a paper quotes an ell infinity radius, check whether it converted or smoothed with a different distribution: uniform or Laplace noise gives an ell one or ell infinity certificate directly.
notes.quote: Different noise, different geometry, same Neyman Pearson skeleton underneath

notes.text: He said the deck is wrong here: the noise scale is sigma, the standard deviation, not the variance sigma squared, and he will fix the slide before posting it.
notes.quote: The noise scale is the standard deviation, not the variance. The deck is wrong there
